$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}g(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{(\pi /4-(-\pi /4))}{\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}(6\operatorname{cos}⁡3x-4\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}(6\operatorname{cos}⁡3x-4\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{2}{\pi }(2\operatorname{sin}⁡3x-4\operatorname{sin}⁡x)|}_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4} \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }[(2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{4})-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}))-(2\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{3\pi }{4})-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{4}))] \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }[(2\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-4\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})-(2\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})-4\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}))] \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }[(-\sqrt{2})-(\sqrt{2})] \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }\cdot (-2\sqrt{2}) \\  & =\frac{-4\sqrt{2}}{\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The number $y(t)$ of people who have adopted electric vehicles in a town follows the logistic growth model

$$
{y}^{′}=4200y-7{y}^{2},\,y(0)=55,
$$

where $t$ is the time, in years, since the observations began. According to this model, what is the maximum possible number of people who will adopt electric vehicles?

The maximum possible number of people who will adopt electric vehicles is
{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
{y}^{′}=ky(a-y),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>y$ is the carrying capacity. 

The carrying capacity $a$ represents the maximum possible number of people who will adopt electric vehicles. A diagram showing a typical logistic growth curve is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224712/assets/d8133f1c4203903bac606bbae61c73717e2ba2dc15a97a77f48eaaeaf4736d06.png)

First, let's rewrite the right-hand side of the given equation so that it matches the form above:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =4200y-7{y}^{2} \\  & =7y(600-y)\end{aligned}
$$

From here, we see that $a=600.$ Hence, the carrying capacity is $600,$ and we conclude that the maximum possible number of people who will adopt electric vehicles is $600.$

questions.problem:
Consider the curve defined parametrically as 

$$
x={e}^{t},\,y=2{e}^{t/2},\,t\in [0,4].
$$

What integral gives the surface area generated when this curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis?
questions.worked_solution:
We can find the surface area generated when a curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis using the formula

$$
S=\int 2\pi y\,\text{d}s.
$$

Since our curve is given in parametric form, we have

$$
\text{d}s=\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Therefore, we will use

$$
S=2\pi {\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

We are told that the limits of integration are from ${t}_{1}=0$ to ${t}_{2}=4.$ 

Computing the derivatives, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})={e}^{t} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{e}^{t/2})={e}^{t/2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =2\pi {\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{4}2{e}^{t/2}\sqrt{{({e}^{t})}^{2}+{({e}^{t/2})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =4\pi {\int }_{0}^{4}{e}^{t/2}\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+{e}^{t}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =4\pi {\int }_{0}^{4}{e}^{t/2}\sqrt{{e}^{t}({e}^{t}+1)}\,\text{d}t \\  & =4\pi {\int }_{0}^{4}{e}^{t/2}\cdot {e}^{t/2}\cdot \sqrt{{e}^{t}+1}\,\text{d}t \\  & =4\pi {\int }_{0}^{4}{e}^{t}\sqrt{{e}^{t}+1}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
For a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ where $n$ is the number of trials, and $p$ is the probability of success on each trial,  we have the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){p}^{x}(1-p)^{n-x}
$$

Here, we have $X∼B(6,0.2),$ so $X$ has the probability mass function

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{x})(0.2)^{x}(0.8)^{6-x}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>4) & =P(X\in \{5,6\}) \\  & =f(5)+f(6) \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{5})(0.2)^{5}(0.8)^{6-5}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{6})(0.2)^{6}(0.8)^{6-6} \\  & =6(0.2)^{5}(0.8)+1(0.2)^{6}(0.8)^{0} \\  & =0.0016.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the arc of the curve $x=-{y}^{2}-5y-4$ that lies in the fourth quadrant between its $y$-intercepts. What integral gives the surface area generated when this arc is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis?
questions.worked_solution:
We can find the surface area generated when a curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis using the formula

$$
S=\int 2\pi x\,\text{d}s.
$$

Since we're given a curve in the form $x=f(y),$ we have 

$$
\text{d}s=\sqrt{1+{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}y.
$$

Therefore, we will use

$$
S=2\pi {\int }_{{y}_{1}}^{{y}_{2}}x\sqrt{1+{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}y.
$$

First, we need to determine the limits of integration. To do this, we find where the curve intersects the $y$-axis by solving the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}-{y}^{2}-5y-4 & =0 \\ {y}^{2}+5y+4 & =0 \\ (y+1)(y+4) & =0 \\ y & =-4,-1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we need to integrate from $y=-4$ to $y=-1.$ 

Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(-{y}^{2}-5y-4)=-2y-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =2\pi {\int }_{{y}_{1}}^{{y}_{2}}x\sqrt{1+{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{-4}^{-1}(-{y}^{2}-5y-4)\sqrt{1+{(-2y-5)}^{2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =-2\pi {\int }_{-4}^{-1}({y}^{2}+5y+4)\sqrt{26+20y+4{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =-2\pi \sqrt{2}{\int }_{-4}^{-1}({y}^{2}+5y+4)\sqrt{2{y}^{2}+10y+13}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
